name: V-KOOL 70
shortDescription: The film chosen by the AIA headquarters and the Guggenheim Museum — 70% VLT, 55% TSER, 94% IR rejection, ~9% exterior reflectance.
description:
V-KOOL 70 (VK70) is the flagship of the V-Kool architectural film series and the most widely specified product in the lineup. It uses V-Kool's proprietary XIR® multi-layer sputtered technology to deliver 55% total solar energy rejection and 94% infrared rejection while transmitting 70% of visible light — a near-clear appearance at a level of solar performance that few films can match at any VLT.

The specification history tells its own story. The American Institute of Architects headquarters in Washington D.C. evaluated multiple window film brands and selected VK70. The Guggenheim Museum in New York integrated V-Kool film into its skylight retrofit to preserve daylight while reducing solar gain and UV exposure on priceless artwork. Exxon specified VK70 for new stores facing high solar load. These are specifications where the visible appearance of the glass was as important as the solar performance — and VK70 met both requirements without compromise.

For Philadelphia buildings, VK70 is the standard first recommendation across a wide range of applications. Class A office towers with architectural glazing specifications, historic buildings in Old City and Society Hill where preservation guidelines restrict darkly tinted or highly reflective coatings, and premium residences on Rittenhouse Square where property value is tied to the appearance of the windows all match the VK70 profile. The exterior reflectance of approximately 9% keeps the building's appearance consistent from the street while the solar performance transforms the interior comfort.

All V-KOOL 70 specifications are NFRC-tested on 3mm single-pane clear glass. Window Film Philadelphia is an authorized V-Kool installer — installations carry a lifetime residential warranty and a 10-year commercial warranty from Eastman.

benefits.heading: Institutional-Grade Specification
benefits.body: VK70 has been chosen by the AIA headquarters, the Guggenheim Museum, and Exxon for specifications where both visible glass appearance and solar performance were non-negotiable. Philadelphia commercial and institutional buildings that meet those same criteria have the same product available.

benefits.heading: Optically Near-Clear at 70% VLT
benefits.body: The 70% visible light transmission and ~9% exterior reflectance keep the glass looking like untreated glass from inside and outside the building — appropriate for Philadelphia historic districts and HOA-governed properties that restrict visible film treatments.

benefits.heading: 94% Infrared Rejection
benefits.body: V-Kool's XIR® sputtered technology reflects infrared radiation rather than absorbing it — the glass itself stays cooler and less secondary heat radiates into the room, a fundamental physics advantage over ceramic solar films.

benefits.heading: Full Warranty Coverage
benefits.body: Lifetime residential warranty; 10-year commercial warranty. Backed by Eastman, V-Kool's parent company and the same manufacturer behind LLumar and Vista.

name: V-KOOL 75
shortDescription: The highest visible light transmission in the V-Kool series — 77% VLT with 45% TSER and 77% IR rejection. For Philadelphia historic and preservation glass.
description:
V-KOOL 75 (VK75) delivers the highest visible light transmission in the V-Kool series — 77% VLT — making it the specification of choice when preserving maximum daylight is the primary requirement and some reduction in solar heat rejection performance is acceptable in exchange. VK75 transmits more visible light than VK70 while still providing 45.45% total solar energy rejection, 77.14% infrared rejection, and 99% UV block. In practical terms, it's the closest V-Kool film to being invisible.

For Philadelphia's historic district properties — Society Hill townhouses, Old City rowhomes, Chestnut Hill residences, and Germantown institutional buildings where preservation guidelines restrict anything that visibly changes the glass — VK75 is effectively undetectable while still providing meaningful UV protection and infrared rejection. The specification is also appropriate for north-facing glass and interior spaces where daylighting is already limited and any reduction in visible light would materially worsen the occupant experience.

Glass-heavy modern residences with expansive views also benefit from VK75. Where VK70 already reads as near-clear from the street, VK75 reads as essentially untreated — the film is present, the UV and infrared protection is real, but from a normal viewing distance nothing about the glass looks different. Philadelphia luxury residential clients who specifically value the connection to their surroundings often choose VK75 for its ability to protect the interior without altering the view.

All V-KOOL 75 specifications are NFRC-tested on 3mm single-pane clear glass. Available through Window Film Philadelphia with the same lifetime residential warranty and 10-year commercial warranty as the rest of the VK series.

benefits.heading: Highest VLT in the Series
benefits.body: 77% visible light transmission — the highest in the V-Kool lineup. Preserves natural daylight for Philadelphia historic properties, north-facing spaces, and view-dependent premium residences.

benefits.heading: Preservation-Compatible
benefits.body: Effectively invisible on the glass from normal viewing distances. Compatible with Philadelphia historic district requirements in Society Hill, Old City, Chestnut Hill, and Germantown that restrict visible coatings.

benefits.heading: Meaningful UV & IR Protection
benefits.body: 99% UV block and 77.14% infrared rejection despite the high VLT — real protection for interior furnishings, artwork, and hardwood floors without altering the appearance of the window.

benefits.heading: NFRC-Tested Specifications
benefits.body: Independently verified performance data on 3mm clear glass per NFRC guidelines. Lifetime residential warranty; 10-year commercial warranty from Eastman.

name: V-KOOL 55
shortDescription: The V-Kool film engineered to meet IECC SHGC 0.40 — 58% VLT with 59% TSER and 96% IR rejection.
description:
V-KOOL 55 (VK55) was developed specifically to meet the International Energy Conservation Code (IECC) requirement of a Solar Heat Gain Coefficient of 0.40. It sits between VK70 and VK40 in the series, delivering 58% VLT, 59% total solar energy rejection, and 96% infrared rejection — measurably better heat rejection than VK70 while maintaining a significantly higher visible light transmission than the darker VK40.

For Philadelphia commercial renovation projects that must demonstrate energy code compliance under the current IECC, VK55 provides the specifiable performance threshold at a shading coefficient of 0.47. The 58% VLT reads as lightly tinted glass rather than dark solar film, which keeps the building's exterior appearance consistent with Philadelphia's architectural standards for commercial glazing on most streets. For south- and west-facing office glass where the afternoon solar load is the primary driver and moderate privacy is a secondary benefit, VK55 delivers noticeably better heat rejection than the flagship VK70.

Property managers overseeing multi-tenant residential buildings in Center City, Fishtown, and Northern Liberties often specify VK55 as a standardized solar control product across mixed-orientation glass. The balanced VLT works acceptably on north- and east-facing units where VK70 might have been the ideal specification and on south- and west-facing units where VK40 might have been chosen — one carefully-chosen film across the entire portfolio simplifies specification, ordering, warranty tracking, and installation logistics.

All V-KOOL 55 specifications are NFRC-tested on 3mm single-pane clear glass. Window Film Philadelphia installs VK55 across residential and commercial applications with lifetime residential and 10-year commercial warranty coverage from Eastman.

benefits.heading: Meets IECC SHGC 0.40
benefits.body: Engineered specifically to meet the International Energy Conservation Code requirement of a Solar Heat Gain Coefficient of 0.40 at a shading coefficient of 0.47 — the film for Philadelphia commercial projects with energy code compliance requirements.

benefits.heading: 96% Infrared Rejection
benefits.body: Measurably better heat rejection than VK70 at 96% IR blocking — appropriate for south- and west-facing Philadelphia commercial glass where the afternoon solar load is the primary driver of HVAC demand.

benefits.heading: Balanced 58% VLT
benefits.body: 58% visible light transmission reads as lightly tinted glass rather than dark solar film. Compatible with Philadelphia commercial architectural standards on most streets while still providing meaningful glare and privacy improvement.

benefits.heading: Portfolio-Compatible
benefits.body: A single specification that works acceptably across mixed-orientation glass in multi-tenant Philadelphia residential and commercial buildings. Simplifies procurement and installation across large portfolios.

name: V-KOOL 40
shortDescription: The performance leader in the V-Kool series — 64.5% TSER and 98.3% IR rejection with 42.8% VLT for glare reduction.
description:
V-KOOL 40 (VK40) is the performance leader in the V-Kool architectural film series. With 64.53% total solar energy rejection and 98.3% infrared rejection, VK40 delivers the most aggressive heat control in the lineup — while maintaining 42.8% visible light transmission, a level that reads as lightly tinted rather than dark. At that VLT, the glass preserves meaningful natural light even as it blocks nearly all of the infrared heat spectrum.

VK40 is the V-Kool specification when glare reduction and maximum heat control are the primary drivers and some visible tinting is acceptable. For Philadelphia's west-facing commercial glass — the Category 1 solar load exposure that creates afternoon hotspots on Center City office floors from noon onward — VK40 resolves the heat and glare problem more completely than any other product in the series. Facilities managers who have tried VK70 or VK55 on severely sun-loaded west-facing floors and found them insufficient often move to VK40 for the additional performance margin.

For residential applications, VK40 addresses rowhomes facing western or southern orientations where afternoon sun makes rooms uncomfortable even after standard solar film installation. Sun-drenched Passyunk Square rooms, west-facing Fishtown living rooms, and south-facing Society Hill sunrooms where fading of hardwood floors and upholstery is a documented problem are appropriate applications for VK40. The 98.3% infrared rejection stops the heat, and the 99% UV block stops the fade.

All V-KOOL 40 specifications are NFRC-tested on 3mm single-pane clear glass. VK40 carries the same lifetime residential warranty and 10-year commercial warranty as the rest of the V-Kool series from Eastman.

benefits.heading: Maximum Heat Rejection in the Series
benefits.body: 64.53% total solar energy rejection and 98.3% infrared rejection — the highest performance V-Kool architectural film. For Philadelphia west-facing glass where afternoon solar load creates hotspots that lower-tier films can't fully resolve.

benefits.heading: Real Glare Reduction
benefits.body: 42.8% VLT delivers meaningful glare reduction on screens and workstations while still transmitting enough light that the space doesn't feel dark. Appropriate for Philadelphia offices with monitor-heavy floors and east/west sun angles.

benefits.heading: Fade Prevention on High-Sun Exposures
benefits.body: 99% UV block plus 98.3% IR rejection stops both the ultraviolet radiation and the infrared heat that drive fade damage — protecting Philadelphia rowhome hardwood floors, upholstery, and artwork on sun-drenched exposures.

benefits.heading: Shading Coefficient 0.42
benefits.body: The lowest shading coefficient in the V-Kool lineup — appropriate for Philadelphia commercial glass with the highest solar load and for building envelope calculations requiring aggressive SHGC reduction.
